title: Retail loan book: early delinquency review

findings.headline: 30-day arrears at 6 months have nearly doubled
findings.detail: The rate of loans 30+ days past due at 6 months rose from 7.2% for Q1 25 loans to 12.8% for Q1 26 loans, up 5.6 points. The rise began in Q3 25 (7.8%), with about 1,000 loans per quarter.

findings.headline: Personal and Card loans drive the deterioration
findings.detail: Personal loans went from 9.3% to 21.0% and Card from 11.2% to 20.2% between Q1 25 and Q1 26. Car (6.1% to 6.3%) and Home (1.1% to 0.5%) were broadly flat.

findings.headline: Shared phone numbers go with very high default and missed first payments
findings.detail: 9 phone values repeat across 42 loans. 83.3% of those loans reached 30+ days past due (about 35 of 42), against 8.8% overall, and 81% missed the first payment. This pattern may point to fraud or linked applications.

findings.headline: Digital and self-employed loans show higher arrears
findings.detail: Digital is at 13.0% against 5.8% for Branch, and Self-employed at 12.2% against 6.5% for Salaried. Digital also has a lower average bureau score (715.4 against 733.7 for Branch), but this does not explain the gap on its own.

findings.headline: Income is missing for 39.7% of Partner loans
findings.detail: Income is missing in 6.9% of rows overall, and 90.8% of those gaps are in the Partner channel. Any affordability analysis would be unreliable for that channel until this is fixed.

next_steps: Review the 42 loans sharing phone numbers with fraud and operations teams, and check applications, addresses and disbursal dates for links.
Split Personal and Card arrears for 2025-2026 by channel, employment and disbursal month to find where the Q4 25 and Q1 26 jump began.
Ask Partner channel owners why income is missing for 39.7% of loans, and decide whether income must be mandatory at application.

reviews.note: Rates 7.2% to 12.8% and +5.6 points are right. 12.8/7.2 is about 1.8 times, so 'nearly doubled' overstated; reworded.
All eight rates match the summary. Changed 'drive' to wording that does not imply cause, and added the Q4 25 step-up.
83.3% of 42 is 35, 81% and 8.8% match. Removed unsupported fraud speculation; noted only 9 phone values are involved.
Rates and bureau scores match. Removed the claim that bureau score does not explain the gap; the summary cannot show that.
6.9%, 90.8% and 39.7% all appear in the summary and are consistent with each other. Medium severity is fair.

findings.headline: 30-day arrears at 6 months rose from 7.2% to 12.8%
findings.detail: The rate was 7.2% for Q1 25 loans and 12.8% for Q1 26 loans, up 5.6 points (about 1.8 times). It was lowest at 6.6% in Q2 25, then rose each quarter: 7.8%, 9.7%, 12.8%. Each quarter has about 1,000 loans.

findings.headline: The rise is in Personal and Card loans
findings.detail: Personal went from 9.3% to 21.0% and Card from 11.2% to 20.2% between Q1 25 and Q1 26, with the biggest steps in Q4 25. Car (6.1% to 6.3%) and Home (1.1% to 0.5%) were broadly flat.

findings.headline: Loans sharing phone numbers have very high arrears
findings.detail: 9 phone values repeat across 42 loans. 83.3% of those loans (about 35 of 42) reached 30+ days past due, against 8.8% overall, and 81% missed the first payment. The group is small, so treat it as a lead to check.

findings.headline: Digital and self-employed loans show higher arrears
findings.detail: Digital is at 13.0% against 5.8% for Branch and 7.2% for Partner. Self-employed is at 12.2% against 6.5% for Salaried. These groups may overlap with the product mix, which this summary does not separate.

findings.headline: Income is missing for 39.7% of Partner loans
findings.detail: Income is missing in 6.9% of rows overall, and 90.8% of those gaps are in the Partner channel. Any income or affordability analysis would be unreliable for that channel until this is fixed.

next_steps: Check the 42 loans sharing phone numbers: compare applications, disbursal dates and first-payment history to see whether they are linked.
Split Personal and Card arrears by channel, employment and disbursal month to find where the Q4 25 and Q1 26 rise began.
Ask Partner channel owners why income is missing for 39.7% of their loans, and decide whether income should be mandatory at application.
conclusion: Early arrears are clearly worsening: 7.2% for Q1 25 loans against 12.8% for Q1 26 loans, and the rise sits in Personal and Card lending while Car and Home are flat. The first thing to do is break down Personal and Card arrears by channel, employment and month to find where the rise started. In parallel, have the 42 loans with shared phone numbers checked, as their arrears are far above the book.
limits: This review uses summary counts and rates only, so it cannot show why arrears are rising, whether Q1 26 loans have had a full six months to be measured, or whether the segment differences overlap.
